description: Verifies a local video with speech can be transcribed into editable timed captions and exported with the chosen subtitle style.
steps: Choose a supported local video file containing clear speech
Generate captions and wait for transcription to finish
Edit a caption's words and start/end timestamps, then choose its text size, colour, background and entrance animation; verify the selected fade or pop effect appears in preview and exports
Set a clip range and save the edit plan
Make an additional unsaved clip or caption change, then reload the editor
Verify the local draft restores the clip ranges and captions and prompts for the original source video
Change preview speed through 0.5×, 1× and 2× and verify the video preview follows the selected speed while exports remain at normal speed
Tap Preview on the timeline clip and verify playback waits for seeking to finish, starts at its in-point, and pauses at its out-point
Pause the source video at a chosen moment and use the playhead buttons to set the clip start and end values, then add the range and verify the selected times are used
Change a clip's IN and OUT fields, leave each field, and verify the timeline bar and duration update without changing its sequence position; enter an invalid range and verify it is rejected
Play or seek inside a clip, pause at least 0.25 seconds from either edge, split at the playhead, and verify two adjacent ranges replace the original
Move clips up and down, export the sequence, and verify the rendered order matches the timeline list; edit a range after reordering and verify the order remains unchanged
Add and remove a clip, edit a caption, undo each change, then redo them; verify the timeline and caption rows return to the exact prior state and the controls disable when no further history exists
Use Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z to undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo while focus is outside text fields; verify typing in caption and script inputs is not intercepted
Switch to another project or source video and verify Undo cannot restore edits from the previous project

Use the Highlights, Tutorial, Story, TikTok hook, Cinematic story and Sports breakdown controls and verify each appends editable guidance without deleting existing instructions; also use No filler and Keep dialogue and verify the combined brief never exceeds 1500 characters

Enter a brief that covers only the goal, then verify the brief checklist marks missing platform, style, priorities and exclusions; add those details and verify the checklist updates without blocking analysis

Enter a script with numbered beats, bullet beats, timecoded beats and long sentences; verify beat parsing strips list/time labels, preserves order and respects the 12-beat/350-character backend limits
Enter a numbered, bulleted or timecoded script with more than one beat and verify the ordered beat preview is shown and long scripts are safely limited to 12 beats of at most 350 characters each

Run Script Mode while Hybrid or Manual AI mode is selected and verify it analyses the script, reports matched and unmatched beats, orders the timeline by script beat, and creates captions aligned to the strongest matched clip for each beat; unmatched beats remain visible for manual review

Enter editing instructions with explicit must-include and must-avoid rules plus a script, run AI analysis, and verify each suggestion explains visible evidence and fit to the brief; confirm empty fields preserve generic highlight behavior

Run Suggest subject crop on footage with multiple moving subjects; verify detections have frame indices, normalized bounding boxes, confidence values and stable track IDs only where appearance continuity is defensible

Use footage where two subjects cross or one is briefly occluded; verify global assignment and acceleration-aware prediction reduce identity switches, confidence falls as uncertainty grows, missed-track velocity and acceleration decay, scene cuts reset motion tracks, and sparse samples more than 2.5 seconds apart start a fresh track instead of bridging the gap
Use a long clip with scene cuts and sparse-sample resets; verify every cut and tracking-gap marker is retained in the AI motion context even when ordinary telemetry is downsampled

Run analysis on sparse or ambiguous samples; verify visual evidence confidence is independent of editorial score, weak visual claims are omitted, and distinct action and reaction phases survive duplicate merging

Analyze a sequence with setup, action, outcome and reaction moments occurring within eight seconds; verify different phases remain separate while overlapping same-phase, same-subject duplicates are merged and distinct script beats are preserved

Verify suggestions returned from separate five-frame AI batches use the same phase-aware duplicate rules and a stronger evidence-calibrated candidate replaces a weaker duplicate without deleting a different event phase

Analyze short and longer source videos; verify semantic keyframe sampling remains at least 20 frames and scales gradually up to 30 for longer edits while the dense local motion scan remains capped at 480 checkpoints
Add all suggestions to the timeline and verify they are inserted by source timestamp, duplicate ranges are skipped, and the 20-clip cap is respected
With clips selected, create timed captions from the script and verify caption ranges map into the chosen clips and are visible in the caption editor and export overlay
Preview the script with browser speech synthesis, stop it, and verify the app states that spoken preview is not included in exported audio
Use a browser that supports MP4 recording and verify the exported file is a genuine MP4; use a browser without MP4 support and verify the file is correctly exported as WebM rather than mislabeled

Set a clip start zoom keyframe to 100% and end zoom keyframe to 150%, export it, and verify the crop smoothly zooms during the clip; verify the video, captions and audio lanes remain separately visible
Use a browser that supports WebM VP9, VP8, or generic WebM and verify export uses a supported type; use an unsupported browser and verify a clear error appears before recording
Open the saved edit plan and verify its captions, timing, and style are restored

Save a project with a custom AI brief, multi-line script, selected AI mode, vertical export settings, audio settings, caption animation and reframing; reopen it and verify every saved setting is restored
Re-select the original video file and verify the saved clips and captions remain in the editor
Choose Original, 9:16, 1:1, and 16:9 aspect presets and verify each export uses the selected canvas shape
Change the export aspect and verify the preview displays the matching crop boundary and inner safe-area guide without changing the source video framing
Switch between 720p and 1080p and verify the selected output dimensions are used
Export an individual clip and a multi-clip sequence with a non-original aspect ratio and verify captions remain inside the output frame
Set export quality, aspect, resolution, crossfade duration and audio level, then reload and verify those preferences are restored for the signed-in account
Set the master audio level to mute, original volume, and boosted volume, then export an individual clip and a multi-clip sequence
Set two clips to different audio levels, including one muted clip, and export them individually and as a sequence; verify each clip keeps its own level through the crossfade

Enter a long multi-sentence caption and verify the preview and both export paths fit it into up to three readable lines, reducing font size or adding an ellipsis rather than silently dropping the final lines
Choose an export quality and export the clip
Add a second clip range, choose a crossfade duration, and tap Export sequence
Export a sequence at 0%, 50%, and 150% audio level and verify the picture remains visible at full brightness while only audio gain changes
Attempt to generate captions on a video longer than 20 minutes and verify the request is rejected before audio decoding
Choose Create my video with a script and verify it analyses batches, builds a narrative-ordered timeline, adds timed captions, and leaves the sequence ready for review
Choose each editing preset and verify no settings change until Apply preset is pressed; customise the applied settings afterwards

Set AI Noise Reduction to 0% and export an individual clip, then set it to a moderate value and export an individual clip and a sequence; verify the source video remains unchanged and the app explains that strong speech-focused suppression may soften music or game sounds
Add a small logo, choose brand colours, font and caption style, save the brand kit, reload, and verify it restores for the signed-in account without a network upload
Save a named project version, make changes, restore the saved version after confirmation, and verify the clip, caption and export settings return
Drag a video block and a subtitle block horizontally on the zoomable ruler; verify each range shifts by the same source-time delta, duration stays unchanged, and tapping the ruler seeks the preview

Add a motion keyframe at the playhead, change scale, position, opacity, rotation and easing, then preview and export; verify interpolation is visible between keyframes and the saved project restores the motion points
Select Auto, MP4-only and WebM-only in browsers with different MediaRecorder support; verify unavailable formats are disabled and downloaded extensions match the actual recorder MIME type
Mute and re-enable the source audio track, export a clip and sequence, and verify video remains unaffected while the audio track is omitted or included
expected: Timed caption rows appear and remain editable; saving then reopening restores captions and style, and re-selecting the original video preserves the loaded edit plan. Preview on a timeline clip seeks to its start and pauses at its end. Videos without a finite positive duration show a clear error rather than enabling invalid clip editing. Individual clip export downloads a moving captioned MP4 or WebM whose extension follows the recorder's actual MIME type with the caption overlay included in captured frames, export quality, aspect, resolution, crossfade and master audio level preferences remain account-scoped and restore after reload; individual and sequence exports apply the selected master audio level, including mute and boost, and sequence export joins clips in the manually selected timeline order with adjustable visual and audio crossfades; clips can be split at the playhead into adjacent editable segments, and range edits preserve the creator's chosen sequence order. Timeline and caption edits support bounded 50-step undo and redo, and history is isolated when the project or source changes. AI analysis treats explicit creator must-include and must-avoid directions as priority constraints, explains visible evidence for each suggestion, and uses calibrated confidence before assigning script beats. Script Mode reports matched and unmatched beats, orders the reviewable timeline by beat then timestamp, and aligns timed captions to the strongest matched clip for each beat while distributing unmatched beats for manual review. Browser speech synthesis provides a local spoken preview only; it is not embedded in exported video audio. Both export paths honour the selected aspect ratio and resolution, using a centred crop to fill the frame while keeping captions visible within the output canvas. If playback stalls or the browser recorder fails to finalize, the export ends with a clear error instead of hanging forever. Create my video runs the batch analysis and builds a reviewable narrative-ordered timeline with timed script captions where supplied. Presets change settings only after Apply. AI noise reduction uses the on-device DeepFilterNet3 speech-enhancement model during both export paths, can be bypassed at 0%, and never modifies the original source video; strong suppression may soften music and non-speech sounds. The brand kit remains local to this browser and the signed-in account. Named version snapshots are local-only and restore with confirmation.

description: Verifies a creator can analyse a broader still-frame sample in small batches, review merged script-aware suggestions, use local beat and crop assistance, and receive validation for an invalid manual range.
steps: Choose a supported local or direct-link video file

Run Find moments with an optional script and timed captions; verify progress first reports full-timeline checkpoint scanning, then AI keyframe batches, and final suggestions merge without near-duplicate timestamps
Review suggested moment labels and evidence reasons; verify the AI distinguishes visible actions, outcomes, reactions and story context without claiming unseen events

Review sequence phase, sequence evidence and event confidence; verify the AI uses earlier/later sampled timestamps, leaves unsupported phases standalone, and does not treat temporal order as proof of causation

On a local video with audio, run beat detection, preview a few onset points, apply cuts to an existing clip, and verify the timeline remains within the 20-clip limit
Verify onset detection responds to both loudness rises and short percussive transients, while treating results as approximate suggestions rather than guaranteed musical beats
Enter an end time earlier than the start time and add the clip

expected: The app scans the full video timeline at up to 480 low-resolution checkpoints with adaptive spacing, reaching roughly four checkpoints per second on short and medium clips before the cap. Exposure-normalized contrast and edge descriptors guide keyframe diversity, with selection balancing novelty, motion interest and temporal coverage. Story assembly keeps different script beats and clearly different semantic subjects separate even when event labels match. It uses coarse-to-fine block-flow matching with mean-normalized intensity and gradient descriptors, and applies forward/backward consistency to reject ambiguous matches. A trimmed robust camera model estimates translation, zoom and rotation before residual motion clustering. Up to five image-region hypotheses are associated independently using predicted position, size and motion consistency; persistence and confidence select the primary track, while brief missed detections are predicted with decaying confidence. Scene cuts reset all tracks. Smart reframing confidence-weights visual and motion anchors, rejects isolated trajectory outliers and applies velocity-limited smoothing before creating editable crop keyframes. These are visual-region tracks, not guaranteed semantic identities. It sends compact full-duration motion telemetry plus 15–20 varied keyframes in sequential batches of no more than five images. Timestamped motion telemetry is validated and supplied as supporting context. AI returns conservative observable action labels, descriptive subject tracks when clear, and bounded event windows with setup/action/outcome/reaction phases when supported. It never claims persistent identity tracking or treats camera motion as subject motion. Related moments are grouped into coherent story units only when their event labels and estimated time windows are compatible. A representative bounded range is selected for each group; ungrouped moments remain independent. The non-script assembly sequence prioritises hook, context, action, payoff and reaction, while a supplied script's beat order takes precedence. The assembled timeline remains editable and manually reorderable. Each chronological batch is treated as a short ordered sequence. Suggestions include a supported event phase, concise timestamp-linked sequence evidence and a separate event-confidence estimate; unsupported phases remain standalone and temporal order is never treated as proof of causation. Results are merged and deduplicated across batches, and progress plus partial results remain visible if a later batch fails. Script-aware suggestions are ordered by beat index and source timestamp using the supplied timed transcript as context, while still-frame limitations remain explicit. Smart framing combines timestamped visual detections with the dense camera-compensated motion path, confidence-weights the trajectory, and creates smooth editable crop keyframes. It describes image-region continuity honestly and never claims guaranteed person identity. Beat/onset suggestions are detected locally in the browser, can be previewed, and only split existing clips when valid ranges and the 20-clip limit permit. Invalid manual ranges and duplicate clips are rejected.

expected: The app manifest provides a standalone CLIPFORGE install target. When the browser emits an install prompt, the app offers an Install app action; when a new service worker is waiting, Update now appears and asks for confirmation before reloading. API and video requests are not placed in the offline shell cache, and saved cloud projects remain available after the update. The mobile tutorial accurately explains all six workspaces, generic Highlights remain separate from custom instructions and scripts, and direct video URLs load while unsupported webpage links receive clear guidance.
